title: POC onramp playlist - tasks, timeline, and acceptance criteria
summary: Working plan and compact task board for customer POC onboarding. Focused on a 6-week onramp with clear acceptance criteria for demo-ready deployment, plus a short workshop agenda and risk register.
objectives: Deliver a production-like POC environment that can serve 50 rps with 99th percentile latency < 300ms for single-turn generation
Demonstrate model variant fallback and routing policy between hosted and dedicated nodes
Validate inference cost estimates and produce a short optimization plan (batching + caching + quantization)
scope_in: Connector integration for customer S3 and internal artifact repo
Model onboarding: open model v1 and a quantized v1-q8 as fallback
Basic observability: latency, token-cost, per-route dashboard
Canary rollout and automatic fallback policy configuration
scope_out: Full production multi-tenant deployment (out of scope for initial POC)
Enterprise-grade IAM / SCIM provisioning (may be included in later dedicated phase)
success_criteria: Demo traffic (synthetic) at 50 rps without errors for 30 minutes
99th percentile generation latency <= 300ms under demo workload
End-to-end request path and fallback exercised in workshop demo
Customer approves initial cost and throughput estimates and signs off on next-phase SOW
timeline_overview: Six-week timeline with three two-week sprints: discovery & infra prep, integration & model tuning, validation & handoff. Key milestone demo at end of week 6.
phases: Phase 0 (pre-onramp, week -1 to 0): Legal/Networking approvals, AWS account linking, KMS key exchange
Sprint 1 (week 1-2): Kickoff, discovery, environment provisioning, initial connector stub
Sprint 2 (week 3-4): Ingest sample data, model onboarding, latency tuning, basic dashboards
Sprint 3 (week 5-6): Load validation, canary rollout, workshop demo, handoff docs and runbook

milestones: M1: Network approvals & account link (end of pre-onramp)
M2: Baseline stack deployed and model verified (end of week 2)
M3: Integration and perf goals hit for alpha traffic (end of week 4)
M4: Workshop demo and sign-off (end of week 6)
acceptance_criteria: Functional: request path returns expected schema for 95%+ of synthetic queries
Reliability: 99.9% success rate during 30-minute demo at 50 rps synthetic traffic
Performance: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 180ms, p99 < 300ms on demo cluster
Operational: dashboards show per-route cost and latency, alerts firing for >5% error spike
Security: customer KMS integration validated and secrets rotated once
workshop_agenda: 10:35 - 11:00 Live demo: baseline vs fallback path, canary (Sofia + Live traffic)
11:00 - 11:20 Interactive: tune a prompt and observe token-cost impact (hands-on)
11:20 - 11:40 Runbook review: support playbook and rollback steps (Ravi)
11:40 - 12:00 Open Q&A, next steps and SOW discussion
risks: Customer network setup delays (firewall/VPC peering) leading to timeline slip
Model artifact incompatible format causing extra conversion work
Quota limits on customer cloud account preventing load testing
Observed latency higher than expected on specific content types
Security review requires additional pen test before demo
mitigation_actions: Start network checklist immediately; request networking POC from customer during week 0
Maintain a lightweight adapter script for artifact conversion (pre-built templates)
Use synthetic hosted load generator to prove behavior if customer quota blocks scale tests
Run targeted microbenchmarks on representative prompts early to detect content hotspots
Offer a short security questionnaire and provide contact for vulnerability triage to accelerate pen test scheduling

notes: This is a working playlist — treat task estimates as T-shirt sizing. Keep the workshop tightly scripted to ensure the fallbacks and routing policies are visibly exercised. After demo, convert tasks to JIRA and attach performance artifacts and Grafana snapshots.
